notes: The Barak's tail numbers and squadron art (shared/aircraft/tail_number.gd, docs/aircraft-models.md §1.6): f16d.glb holds neither (tools/f16/barak.py paints the fin plain, as F-16D 034's camouflage).
notes.number: 034, F-16D Block 30 of 109 Squadron ("The Valley", Ramat David), the player's: its left side in Wikimedia Commons' F-16D--Our-IDF-2018-IZE-239.jpg (2018); the sim's unit record shows the same (modern-iaf/data/db/units/f16d.json `tail`)
notes.others: the other F-16Ds in service in f-16.net's airframe database (docs/aircraft-models.md §1.6, checked 19 Nov 2026), each squadron's in number order: 109 Squadron's (the player's), then Ramat David's other F-16D squadron, 105 (Block 40); then 612, its squadron open (f-16.net's last unit for it, 110 Squadron, closed in 2017). Commons photos show 027, 034 and 074 in 109's art, 667 and 682 in 105's. Not listed: written off (031, 077, 606, 621, 660) and the test centre's 020 and 601
notes.marks: 612's (its squadron open): the number alone, in 109's style
notes.squadrons: each squadron's jets (`tails`) and what they wear, measured on the photos laid onto our fin (y up, z aft, m). 109: the number in thin black digits low on the fin under the eagle (034's: 0.31 m tall, 0.185 m apart, foot 1.04 m up, 4.91 m aft), its pale eagle and red badge (art/f16d_109.svg). 105: bold black digits low at the leading edge (682's: 0.42 m, 0.25 m apart), its pale scorpion and oval badge (art/f16d_105.svg), a red and white chevron on each side of the tail box, flatter than the jets' to fit our shorter box (0.39 × 0.15 m; art/f16d_105_chevron.svg). The art is ours, drawn over the photos; mirrored on the right side, so it faces forward on both
